title: PM-2025-02: Dedicated staged rollout gate evaluator lag (dogfood incident)
author: Rafael Mendes
body:
## Summary
On 2025-02-13, during internal dogfooding of **Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools**, a rollout advanced to Stage 2 (25%) while the **gate evaluator service** was experiencing processing lag. The evaluator did not evaluate gate windows within the expected cadence, delaying an automatic hold that should have occurred when queue depth and p95 latency exceeded thresholds. As a result, the Dedicated pool continued receiving increased traffic allocation for ~17 minutes after conditions should have triggered a pause.

This incident did **not** affect external customers; it impacted an internal dedicated pool used for performance and rollout validation. However, the failure mode is directly relevant to enterprise Dedicated tenants (high-SLA environments), and we are treating this as a priority reliability gap before beta enablement.

**Primary failure mode:** gate evaluation lag + insufficient “stop-the-line” safeguards meant stage advancement and continued routing could outpace gate enforcement.

---

## Impact
**Services affected:**
- Dedicated pool: `ded-pool-dogfood-usw2-07` (internal)
- Gate evaluator service: `rollout-gate-evaluator` (control-plane job/service)
- Routing: `dedicated-router` (stage-weight enforcement)

**User impact:**
- Elevated tail latency and timeouts for internal test workloads routed to the pool
- Rollout did not pause at the intended time, increasing the duration of degraded performance

**Severity:** SEV-2 (internal) / “SEV-1 potential” if this failure mode occurred in an enterprise Dedicated pool.

**Duration:** 10:04–10:29 PT (25 minutes total), with the key “delayed hold” window ~10:08–10:25 PT.

**Key metrics observed:**
- p95 latency: baseline ~420–520 ms → peaked at ~1.9–2.4 s
- Timeout rate: baseline <0.2% → peaked at ~2.8%
- Queue depth: baseline ~0–3 → sustained 25–60
- GPU utilization: sustained 92–98% (limited headroom)

---

## Detection
**How we detected:**
- SRE on-call received an alert for sustained queue depth on the dogfood pool.
- Console rollout view showed Stage 2 (25%) “In Progress” with stale gate evaluation timestamps.

**What should have detected earlier:**
- We lacked a page/alert specifically for **gate evaluator lag** tied to “active rollouts”.
- Existing evaluator health metrics were present but not wired to paging thresholds for this environment.

---

## Timeline (PT)
> Note: timestamps are approximate; derived from on-call notes, alert history, and service logs.

- **10:02** — Operator starts a dogfood rollout plan for `ded-pool-dogfood-usw2-07` (Stage 1: 5% for 10 min, Stage 2: 25% for 15 min). Default gates enabled: p95 latency, 5xx/timeout rate, queue depth, GPU utilization.
- **10:04** — Stage 1 becomes active. Gate evaluator is running but begins accumulating backlog (later correlated with metrics query latency + retry behavior).
- **10:08** — Pool queue depth crosses the Stage 1 queue depth gate threshold for the first time. Expected behavior: evaluator should fail the gate and auto-hold within the evaluation window.
- **10:11** — Stage 2 activates (25%). Console shows “last evaluated” timestamp lagging by ~8–10 minutes, but this is not surfaced as a warning state in the stage UI.
- **10:12** — Alert triggers: sustained queue depth > 20 for 5 minutes. SRE on-call begins investigation.
- **10:15** — p95 latency breaches gate threshold; timeout rate begins trending upward.
- **10:18** — SRE notes evaluator log warnings: slow metric queries + repeated retries. The rollout is still progressing because stage advancement had already occurred and routing continues to apply Stage 2 weight.
- **10:21** — Manual intervention: operator pauses rollout via internal tooling (abort/hold) and reduces stage weight to 0% for the new variant.
- **10:25** — Gate evaluator catches up; it would have transitioned the rollout to HOLD due to queue depth/p95 latency failures. This occurs after manual pause has already been applied.
- **10:29** — Pool returns to baseline queue depth and p95 latency.
- **10:47** — Initial incident debrief in #eng-sre and #eng-platform. Decision: treat evaluator lag as a release-blocking issue for beta.

---

## Root cause
The **gate evaluator** fell behind real time because it was performing metric queries for active rollouts serially with retry-on-timeout behavior, and it encountered degraded query latency from the metrics backend during a period of elevated cardinality for dogfood testing. This led to:

1) **Stale gate decisions** (evaluation timestamps lagging by minutes), and
2) **Delayed hold/rollback enforcement**, allowing routing weights to remain at an unsafe stage longer than intended.

In short: **the system assumed evaluator results were timely, but there was no strong guarantee or enforcement mechanism to prevent stage progression/continued traffic allocation when evaluator freshness degraded.**

---

## Contributing factors
### 1) Missing “freshness” gate / stop-the-line behavior in routing
- Routing continued to enforce the latest stage weights even when evaluator freshness was degraded.
- The UI did not clearly indicate that gates were “unknown/stale” in a way that would block advancement or trigger an operator workflow.

### 2) Retry behavior amplified evaluator lag
- Metric query timeouts retried with insufficient backoff/jitter.
- Retries were not bounded per rollout/stage, increasing queueing inside the evaluator.

### 3) Metrics query patterns were more expensive than expected
- Dogfood load used multiple routes and model versions, increasing the number of queries per evaluation cycle.
- Some dimensions were higher-cardinality than intended for dedicated pools, causing slower aggregation.

### 4) Alerting gaps
- We had alerts for pool symptoms (queue depth/latency) but not for evaluator lag as a **first-class rollout safety signal**.

### 5) Capacity/headroom constraints on the dogfood pool
- The dedicated pool had limited headroom (sustained 90%+ GPU utilization), so a 25% traffic shift was enough to cause immediate queuing.

---

## What went well
- Queue depth alerting worked and paged quickly.
- SRE and platform engineering were able to correlate symptoms with evaluator lag within ~10 minutes.
- Manual pause tooling was effective and reduced impact duration.

## What didn’t go well
- The system did not fail safe when evaluator freshness degraded (should have paused advancement and/or forced HOLD).
- Console did not surface evaluator staleness prominently; it appeared as a “normal” stage in progress.
- Evaluator performance characteristics under load were not load-tested prior to dogfooding Stage 2+.

## Where we got lucky
- This occurred on an internal pool (dogfood), not an enterprise tenant.
- The operator was online and able to apply a manual pause quickly.

---

## Corrective and preventive actions
> Status definitions: **P0** (required before beta), **P1** (required before GA), **P2** (nice-to-have).

| ID | Priority | Action item | Owner | Due date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI-1 | P0 | Implement evaluator freshness checks: if evaluation lag > X minutes for an active stage, set stage state to **UNKNOWN** and force HOLD (no automatic advancement). | Logan Wright | 2025-02-28 | In progress |
| AI-2 | P0 | Routing guardrail: when stage state is UNKNOWN (or evaluator degraded), cap stage weight at current safe value and prevent increases; optionally revert to previous stable variant. | Mina Haddad | 2025-03-07 | Not started |
| AI-3 | P0 | Add alerting + dashboard panels for evaluator lag and evaluation success rate, scoped to “active rollouts”. Page SRE when lag breaches threshold. | Allison Grant | 2025-03-01 | In progress |
| AI-4 | P0 | Bound retries and add exponential backoff + jitter in evaluator metric queries. Add per-rollout budgets to prevent starvation. | Thomas Baird | 2025-02-28 | Not started |
| AI-5 | P1 | Reduce query cost: pre-aggregate low-cardinality dedicated rollout metrics (queue depth, utilization, timeouts) into rollup series tuned for gates. | Caleb Johnson | 2025-03-15 | Not started |
| AI-6 | P1 | Console UX: show explicit warning state when gate results are stale/missing; require manual approval to continue if freshness warning is present. | Kenji Nakamura | 2025-03-15 | Not started |
| AI-7 | P1 | Load test evaluator under worst-case “N pools × M routes × K gates” and validate evaluation SLA. Publish capacity guidance. | Keiko Yamamoto | 2025-03-22 | Not started |
| AI-8 | P2 | Add “evaluation SLA” SLO for rollout safety services (evaluator tick + query latency) and incorporate into release checklist. | Sean Gallagher | 2025-04-05 | Not started |

---

## Follow-up: policy and process changes
- **Beta readiness gate:** Staged rollouts cannot be enabled for an enterprise Dedicated tenant unless evaluator freshness guardrails and alerting are in place (AI-1 through AI-3).
- **Runbook update:** Add a dedicated section: “Gate results stale / evaluator lag” with immediate mitigation steps (pause rollout, reduce weights, confirm metric freshness). (Owner: Rafael Mendes, due 2025-02-21)
- **Release checklist:** Add a pre-flight check in the rollout launch checklist verifying evaluator health dashboards + alerts are green for the target region/pool.

---

## Appendix
### A) Expected behavior vs actual behavior
**Expected:**
- If queue depth/p95 latency exceeds thresholds for the evaluation window, evaluator triggers HOLD within minutes.
- If metrics are missing/late, system fails safe (pause/hold) rather than proceeding.

**Actual:**
- Evaluator lagged and did not produce timely gate results.
- Stage advanced and routing weights increased despite stale evaluation state.

### B) Notes on thresholds in use (dogfood defaults)
- Queue depth gate: HOLD if queue_depth_p95 > 15 for 5 minutes
- Latency gate: HOLD if p95_latency_ms > 1200 for 5 minutes
- Timeout gate: HOLD if timeout_rate > 1.0% for 5 minutes
- Utilization gate: HOLD if gpu_util_p95 > 95% for 10 minutes

(See: Dedicated rollouts gating SLOs page for the authoritative defaults and tuning guidance.)

### C) Communication
- Incident summary posted in #eng-sre and #eng-platform at 10:47 PT.
- Action items tracked under the Dedicated staged rollouts initiative epic and linked to evaluator/routing workstreams.
